findings.claim: The timestamp writer mask changed from 0xffffffff00000000 to 0x00000000ffffffff. The original checked that the upper 32 bits were zero, which selects the 4-byte timestamp32 format. The new check tests whether the lower 32 bits are zero. As a result, ordinary timestamps with non-zero seconds fall through to the 8-byte timestamp64 path, and values that actually fit in 32 bits are written in a different layout. Values with zero low bits but non-zero high bits (nanoseconds<<34 set) would be wrongly emitted as timestamp32 with truncated data, corrupting the DateTime. This is a serialization data-corruption regression in the runtime and is unrelated to the feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize DateTime with non-zero nanoseconds and seconds having zero low 32 bits (e.g. 2^32 seconds plus 1ms) via MessagePackPrimitives.WriteTimestamp, then deserialize and assert round-trip equality. Also byte-diff a plain timestamp against the base build.
